DEFINITION · qeva:1:parity@2

Parity

Classification of integers by their remainder modulo 2.

editorialnumber · arithmetic
Run a related experimentTrace this conceptSearch connections

PLAIN

The idea

Every integer belongs to one of two classes: even or odd.

EXACT

The compact statement

For n in Z: n is even iff there exists k in Z with n=2k. n is odd iff there exists k in Z with n=2k+1.

Example

18 is even because 18=2·9. 19 is odd because 19=2·9+1.

Boundary / caveat

Parity here is the modulo-two classification of integers; it does not make every two-state distinction an arithmetic parity.
